summary: Pure JavaScript OCR library that reads text from images in 100+ languages, in the browser or on Node.js.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Tesseract.js is a JavaScript library that gets words out of images in almost any language. It works in the browser with webpack, ESM or a CDN script tag, and on the server with Node.js.
sixtySeconds.problem: Adding OCR to a web app usually means running a separate server. Tesseract.js runs text recognition directly in JavaScript.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the most widely used JavaScript OCR library, with simple async APIs and many community examples.
requirements: Node.js with npm or yarn, or a browser

overview: Install with npm or yarn, or load it from a CDN with a script tag (an ESM build is also available).
Create a worker for a language, call recognize on an image URL or file, read the text from the result, and terminate the worker.
Community projects include Scribe OCR and examples for PDFs, Electron and TypeScript. Tesseract.js is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Slower than native OCR for large batches
